subject: Materials Science
title: Fractography: Reading Broken Surfaces
description: A short lesson to help you apply Fractography: Reading Broken Surfaces.

hook.text: A broken bolt tells a story — the fracture surface reveals how and why it failed.

buildup.text: Fractography examines fracture surfaces under a microscope to identify the failure mechanism.

discovery.text: Beach marks on a fracture surface signal fatigue. Cleavage facets mean brittle fracture. Dimples mean ductile.

twist.text: The fracture origin — where the crack started — is usually a machining mark, inclusion, or corrosion pit.

climax.text: Crash investigators use fractography to determine if a component failed before or during the accident.

punchline.text: Every fracture surface is a crime scene — and the evidence is in the texture.

quiz.question: What do beach marks on a fracture surface indicate?
options: Fatigue crack growth over many cycles
